# Region Hovedstaden — Hovedstaden

The Capital Region of Denmark is represented in the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (AKDB) through two logically mapped entities: **Region Hovedstaden**, which functions as the administrative and organizational reporting unit, and **Hovedstaden**, which serves as the geographical and demographic identifier for the region's hospitals and patient populations. Together, they provide a comprehensive picture of acute surgical quality and outcomes in the capital area.

As an organization, Region Hovedstaden is one of the five Danish regions that report data to the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]], which is published by the [[regionerne-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]] [^src1]. The region has actively improved its data submission, increasing its reporting frequency from approximately 65% to 75% over a two-year period [^src2]. It also provides regional commentary on the annual reports [^src2], with the 2024 commentary highlighting specific localized variances where proportions ranged from 4.3% to 33.1% within the region's own sub-units [^src6].

Geographically and structurally, Hovedstaden encompasses several major healthcare facilities, including [[amager-og-hvidovre-hospital|Amager og Hvidovre Hospital]], [[bispebjerg-og-frederiksberg-hospitaler|Bispebjerg og Frederiksberg Hospitaler]], [[herlev-og-gentofte-hospital|Herlev og Gentofte Hospital]], [[hospitalerne-i-nordsjaelland|Hospitalerne i Nordsjælland]], and [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] [^src8]. (Note: [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] is occasionally listed under the region in raw data tables, though it is geographically located in [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] [^src8]). As a region within [[danmark|Danmark]], Hovedstaden's patient demographics, such as [[alder|alder]] and [[asa-score|ASA]] score, show no significant differences when compared to other regions like [[midtjylland-region-i-alt|Midtjylland]], [[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland]], [[region-sjaelland|Sjælland]], and [[syddanmark-region-i-alt|Syddanmark]] [^src5] [^src11].

The region's performance across various clinical indicators highlights both strengths and areas of variance. For [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], Hovedstaden achieved a compliance rate of 31.8% (95% CI: 29.0–34.7) for the period of September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023 [^src7], which improved to 33.1% (95% CI: 30.2–36.1) in the subsequent period from September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024 [^src12]. The region also recorded the highest regional fulfillment for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] (nutrition) at 32.4% [^src9]. Conversely, for [[indikator-5y|Indikator 5y]], Region Hovedstaden showed the highest national proportion at 19.9%, compared to 9.0% in [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] [^src1]. Additional 2024 cohort data noted 163 out of 1,012 cases meeting particular clinical criteria [^src4].

Other indicators reveal significant regional disparities across Denmark. For [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]], results varied from 4.3% in Region Hovedstaden to 18.1% in [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] [^src3]. Similarly, for [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]], the proportion ranged from 6.8% in [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] to 33.1% in Region Hovedstaden [^src13]. Regarding patient outcomes, 36 out of 396 patients in Hovedstaden with a [[charlson-score-1-2|Charlson Score = 1 eller 2]] died within 30 days after acute surgery, representing a mortality rate of 9.1% [^src10]. Furthermore, a supplementary indicator ([[indikator-5x|supplerende indikator 5x]]) showed that 80 out of 406 patients (19.7%) were operated on within 6 hours for perforation, ischemia, or bleeding [^src8].
